Child Protection Register II

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
This is a follow on to the programme I made on the Child Protection Register in 2011.
Durban Drama Teacher
A prominent Durban drama teacher who has taught at a string of top KwaZulu-Natal high schools – and directed or performed in numerous drama productions – has been arrested for sexual abuse and possession of child pornography.
The 48-year-old man, who has taught at private and top state schools in Durban and Pietermaritzburg, is alleged to have recruited young boys to make pornography. Although the schools cannot be named at this stage, he is known to have worked at at least six since the early 2000s.
Two teenagers from the same Durban high school have given police signed statements implicating their former teacher in allegations that he used them to create child pornography in return for money. Two more children have also come forward.
One of these case studies will give us an interview.
However this is not his first brush with the law, the teacher was convicted in 2003 for incidents of indecent assault that happened more than 20 years ago, while he was teaching at another school in greater Durban.
He was sentenced to five years, suspended for three years, and to 18 months correctional supervision. Police believe there was “similar grooming” in both incidents although they will only call his earlier victim if he is convicted again and evidence is needed in aggravation of sentence.
The teacher was not checked against the Child Protection Register and there are allegations that the school in question was informed of his previous conviction but hired him anyway.
Although schools are meant to check the teachers against the Child Protection Register it seems that this is not being done.
There are three issues here;
- If the school was informed of his criminal past and hired him knowingly are they legally responsible?
- The Child Protection Register is still not working
- What is the sexual age of consent? The law says that it is 16 but the Child Protection Register says 18. If the children were 16 when the abuse started can the teacher still be charged?

- Victim Case Study
- School
- Joan van Niekerk ( Childline who is involved in this case)
- Marc Hardwick ( who runs an agency that screens schools)
- Prinicipal of School that has been verified or accredited
- Government

Press Release:


Child Protection Register
A prominent Durban drama teacher was recently sentenced to three years imprisonment after being convicted of 230 counts relating to child pornography and sexual exploitation of children. But this is not his first brush with the law. Twelve years ago he was convicted of the indecent assault of a minor. However, this conviction went unnoticed and he was appointed to teaching positions at top schools. Why wasn’t his name added to the Child Protection Register? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


Child Protection Register Script 2015 7 October


V/O

This is Colin Chapman, a 50 year old drama teacher who has come to Durban Regional Court with his bag packed, because he knows he won’t be going home today.

He has been charged with 230 counts of possession of child pornography, the creation of child pornography, the sexual exploitation of a child, the sexual grooming of children and using children for or benefitting from Child Pornography. This is Chapman’s second conviction. Steve was the victim on his first conviction and has come to see justice served.

Steve
“I can’t wait to see his face, just that he knows that I am still here, I am not going anywhere and I will still keep following him until he is taken off the school roll.”

V/O
Steve is 40 years old now, but when he was 14, he was sexually abused by Colin Chapman, who was teaching at Hillcrest High.

Steve
“I remember the first time, it really, really happened was when we were at his house , and we had been watching movies and things, he suddenly just came onto me and he just started giving me a blow job. I wasn’t expecting it, I didn’t ask for it – it just happened.”

V/O
For this crime, Chapman was convicted in 2003 for the indecent assault of a minor for which he was handed a five year suspended sentence. He stopped teaching at Hillcrest High, but spent no time in jail and was not compelled to attend rehabilitation for sexual offenders either.

Steve
“When my Mom found out about it she went to the school counselor. They did ask him to leave eventually. But his name was name was still not taken off the teacher’s roll.”

V/O
Colin Chapman continued to teach at many prestigious schools in the Durban area. At every new school Steve says that he would phone them to warn them about him.

“Some of the schools were grateful and other schools did not want to hear my story and they just said we know about it, he’s under supervision I think their words were that is where it ended.”

V/O
Steve was doing what the Child Protection Register was meant to do, to protect children from abuse. In 2005 the new Children’s Act was passed and it created provision for a register that listed the names of people who were convicted of abusing or ill treating minors.

Link
So how do you know that the people who have access to your children are not sexual predators, not just the teachers, the security guards, the temps, the cleaners, how safe is your child at school?

V/O
In August 2011, Social Development Minister Bathabile Dlamini responded to a question in parliament and revealed that although the Child Protection Register had been fully operational for 16 months , that it had only 1 name on it. This in a country where there are over 50 000 cases of child abuse reported every year.

Joan
“To me it is unconscionable that government should make legislation and yet their own departments do not honour it.”

V/O
Joan van Niekerk is the President of the
International Society for the Prevention of Child Abuse and Neglect and says that our conviction rate in South Africa is very low with the result that very few offenders go onto a register.

Joan
“One of the problems with registers are that it is feel good legislation. The fact of the matter is only a very tiny proportion , less than 1 percent of all offenders who have committed an offence against a child will ever go on a register in this country.”

V/O
Although Colin Chapman was convicted of indecent assault in 2003, he continued to teach children until his arrest in 2014.

Link
To complicate matters, the system is designed in a way that seems to duplicate itself, because there are in fact three registers ; for crimes against Children, there’s the Child Protection Register, for sexual offences there’s the sexual offenders’ register and then there’s the police register which is meant to record all of these crimes and for an administrator it can all be very confusing.


V/O
Marc Hardwick was formerly with the Police Child Protection Unit but now runs an independent company called The Guardian that screens people who work with children.

Bongani
“Are schools more likely to have screened their people or less likely?”

Marc
“I think if we throw all school into the pot independent and government I would say far less likely to have done it.”

Bongani
“Would screening have picked this accused perpetrator.”

Marc
“Yes, absolutely. The fact that he has a previous conviction it would have and it would have alerted the employer to whether they should employ him or not.”

V/O
Steve says he phoned Durban High School three times to warn them about Chapman .

Steve
“I spoke to the Headmaster and he was the one who said we know about it now, he’s under supervision and we will make sure nothing happens.’

V/O
But that was not to be. Greg was a pupil of Colin Chapman’s at DHS.

Greg
“Yes, he was,he was flirtatious he would often make sexual remarks or wink at you during class.”

V/O
Chapman befriended Greg on BBM when he was only 16 years old and that is when the requests started.

Greg
‘It would start with take a picture with your undies on, get an erection and then send me that picture, and that’s how it progressed.”

V/O
Greg’s family was going through financial difficulties and the teacher gained his trust by giving him money.

Greg
“Eventually he got to the stage where he said he was getting bored of it and he had asked me to perform live and he had offered me R 3500 to do that . Considering the money I did comply. So I went to his house where I took my clothes off.”

Bongani
“So he was also undressed?”

Greg
“Yes, he was, he wanted to interact with me at the time as well.”

Bongani
“So he was touching you?”

Greg
“Yes, he was. He perform oral sex on me on that occasion.”

V/O
Greg alleges that over a 6 month period the teacher paid him in excess of R 35 000 for pictures and sexual acts.

V/O
Since Carte Blanche’s first programme on the Child Protection Register in 2011 the amount of people on the the list has increased. Musa Mbere from the Department of Social Development is the manager of the Child Protection Register.

Bongani
“Has that situation changed?”

Musa
“Yes, it has changed we have 555 people to date on that register.”

Bongani
“So in terms of offences recorded how far back do they go?”

Musa
“According to the act they are supposed to go five years back prior the promulgation to the Act of 2010. But because of the way the systems were set up we did not have that information from the South African Police Services.

V/O
It is highly likely that there are many other sex offenders like Colin Chapman who have fallen through the beaurocratic cracks and are not on the register.

V/O
Joan van Niekerk was called in as a court expert for Chapman’s first conviction . She was director of Childline at the time.

Bongani
“When you interviewed him, was it your sense that he could be rehabilitated?”

Joan
“I think at that stage if he had been placed in a programme, there would have been a reduced risk in terms of re offence.”

Bongani
“So when you then heard that there were new allegations what was your response?”

Joan
“Well the writing was on the wall.”

Link
The general consensus is that while paedophilia may be tempered it can’t be cured. THIs was the very reason why the register was started, was to prevent people who have abused children having further access to them.

V/O
The South African Council of Educators or SACE is a professional council for teachers in the country. Matseliso Dipholo, the Chief Operating Officer, believes that checking against the Child Protection Register is voluntary.

Bongani
“As we sit here as far as SACE is concerned there is no legislation that compels employers to check these registers?”

Matseliso
“No, there is nothing.”

Bongani
“We did an investigation at a number of Durban schools and many of them didn’t know…

V/O Interjection follow on with the previous sentence….that they had to check their teachers against the Child Protection Register–

Bongani
does that surprise you?”

Matseliso
“Not really, not really because as I am saying it has not been a focus in South Africa to say when you employ an educator you have to go through this particular process. “

Bongani
“Have you had a directive from any department to screen teachers?”

Joe
“Bongani at this stage we have had no directive from the government what so ever, it’s an initiative that we have taken on upon ourselves to make sure our teachers have been screened. “

V/O
Joe Erasmus is the principal of Ashton International College in Ballito. and believes that the safety of children is paramount.


Joe
“It’s a moral obligation for any school any institution where there is a collection of children getting together that the employer needs to follow a due process wrt to screening those teachers.

Bongani
“We spoke to the South African Council of Educators and its something they encourage but it’s not mandatory.”

Musa
“No, they know it is mandatory. I am sorry to say that, they are aware because there have been several meetings with them.”

V/O
But who carries the responsibility when things do go wrong, as they did at Durban High School?

Leon Erasmus is the new principal and says that as an employee of the KwaZulu Natal Education Department he is not able to talk to us.

Link
But in a statement he says he was shocked to learn of the charges against Colin Chapman ,who could neither confirm nor deny the school had been warned about him, but says that they have since reviewed their teacher screening procedures.

Bongani
“Could schools’s face prosecution if they fail to pick that up?”

Marc
“Yes, if they fail to check there can be prosecution, that would be dependent on the NPA. Legislation says that you can go to prison for up to 7 years for failing to check a staff member.”

V/O
While there seems to be confusion all round the children are the ones who are being affected. Greg is the one who is going to have to deal with the emotional fall out of the abuse.









Bongani
“Do you think the school could have done more to help prevent this?”

Greg
“Knowing that I am paying my school fees and I supposed to be there to have been getting an education. I would have expected them to do a background search on the teacher.”

Marc
“I think parents should be contacting their schools and saying by the by have you checked everybody that is teaching my child. “

V/O
Chapman pleaded guilty to all 230 charges and has been given a 3 year sentence. He has been declared unfit to work with children and his name will now be placed on the Child Protection Register and the Sex Offenders register. But Steve it won’t undo the past.

“There is definitely damage and I have been destroyed.”

2 x 15 seconds
1 x 10 seconds


Promo 1 - 15 sec

How do you know that your children are taught by educators who don’t have a history of sexual abuse? In most cases you don’t. Even though legislation has made it compulsory many schools still do not know that they have to screen their employees against the Child Protection Register.

Promo 2 – 15 sec

How did Colin Chapman, a drama teacher in Durban, continue to teach and exploit children even though he had a previous conviction of indecent assault of a minor? Have all the teachers who teach your children been screened against the Child Protection Register.


Promo 3 – 10 secs

Colin Chapman continued teaching for over 10 years after his first conviction of indecent assault of a minor. Why are sex offenders allowed access to our children?

However this is not his first brush with the law, the teacher was convicted in 2003 for incidents of indecent assault that happened more than 20 years ago, while he was teaching at another school in greater Durban. He was sentenced to five years, suspended for three years, and to 18 months correctional supervision. Police believe there was “similar grooming” in both incidents although they will only call his earlier victim if he is convicted again and evidence is needed in aggravation of sentence. The teacher was not checked against the Child Protection Register and there are allegations that the school in question was informed of his previous conviction but hired him anyway. Although schools are meant to check the teachers against the Child Protection Register it seems that this is not being done. There are three issues here; - If the school was informed of his criminal past and hired him knowingly are they legally responsible? - The Child Protection Register is still not working - What is the sexual age of consent? The law says that it is 16 but the Child Protection Register says 18. If the children were 16 when the abuse started can the teacher still be charged?
